words.g: n. dat. sg. of रक्षण (√रक्ष् + lyuṭ); dative of purpose, parallel to वधाय in 4.41
m. gen. pl. of लोक; depends on रक्षणाय
m. gen. pl. of देव; depends on उपकारिणी
f. nom. sg. of उपकारिन् (उप + √कृ + ṇini, feminine in -ī); qualifies सा (4.41)
pronoun तद्, n. acc. sg.; object of शृणुष्व; takes up the यथा clauses of 4.41–42
√श्रु (svādi, 5P ‘to hear’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, ātmanepada ending — an epic (ārṣa) form for classical शृणु
first-person pronoun अस्मद्, instr. sg.; agent of आख्यातम्
past passive participle (kta) of आ + √ख्या (adādi, 2P ‘to tell’), n. acc. sg.; qualifies तत्
√कथ् (curādi, 10 ‘to tell’), laṭ (present), uttama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada; present for the immediate future
second-person pronoun युष्मद्, enclitic dat. sg.

sandhi.type: anusvāra sandhi; m before a vowel
sandhi.note: Final m before the consonant d becomes anusvāra (लोकानां); before the vowel u it stays m and is written joined (देवानामुपकारिणी).
Final t becomes the palatal c next to the palatal ś, and ś after a stop becomes ch: tac + chṛṇuṣva.
ā + ā → ā; the Gita Press marks the merged long ā with a double avagraha (ऽऽ), as in तथाऽऽत्मनः (4.39).
Final t stays unvoiced before the unvoiced k; the words are only written together.

morph.note: Imperative of √श्रु (stem शृणु-, with the class-5 nu) with the ātmanepada ending -sva (ṣ after u): शृणुष्व. Classical Sanskrit has only the parasmaipada शृणु; the ātmanepada form is common in epic and Purāṇic verse.
Present of the curādi stem कथय-. A present used of what the speaker is about to do stands for the near future: ‘I am going to tell’.
उप + √कृ + ṇini (habitual agent), feminine उपकारिणी: ‘one who habitually helps’.
आ + √ख्या + kta: आख्यात, ‘told’. With मया: ‘(that) told by me’, i.e. as I tell it.

mantras.anvaya: (सा) च लोकानां रक्षणाय देवानाम् उपकारिणी (यथा अभवत्), तत् मया आख्यातं शृणुष्व; (अहं) ते यथावत् कथयामि।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line ends the indirect question begun in 4.41 (‘how she came to be … for the protection of the worlds, the helper of the gods’). तत् takes up the whole of it as the object of शृणुष्व; a short main clause follows (यथावत् कथयामि ते).
mantras.lit: and for the protection of the worlds, the helper of the gods — hear that, told by me; I tell it to you as it was.
mantras.tr: and to protect the worlds, ever the helper of the gods. Listen as I tell it; I shall tell it to you just as it happened.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Ever’ renders the habitual sense of the ṇini affix in उपकारिणी; the future ‘shall tell’ renders the present कथयामि of imminent action.

comm.t: The last mantra of chapter 4 and of the Madhyama Carita. Medhas finishes announcing the third story — the Goddess’s rising from Gaurī for the slaying of Śumbha and Niśumbha and for the protection of the worlds — and promises to tell it exactly. Chapter 5 begins it.
In the Gita Press pāṭha the chapter closes with the recitation bījas ह्रीं ॐ, printed after the verse. They belong to the pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa, and are not part of the verse’s words.

flags.uncertain: Not a doubt about the reading but about the data: text.json stores the closing bījas ह्रीं ॐ inside the second line (…कथयामि ते॥ ह्रीं ॐ॥) instead of in a bija_close field, as every other chapter’s closing bījas are stored. They are not analysed here, so the padaccheda rejoins to the verse but not to the stored line.
